description: The physics layers of the project, read from its scenes, offline. Use it when something falls through the floor, a bullet or pickup is not detected, body_entered never fires, or before you set any collision_layer or collision_mask. Without arguments: per physics world (2D, 3D) every layer in use with its name and bit value, how many nodes are on it and how many scan it; every body, area, ray and TileSet physics layer with its layers and mask as numbers, names and value (instances and inherited scenes resolved); and what can never work: a mask that scans a layer nothing is on (also the classic collision_mask = 3 meant as layer 3, which is the value 4), an area or ray with mask 0, an Area with monitoring off whose body_entered is connected, a body or area without a collision shape, a CollisionShape without a shape; plus the lines of code that change layers. `between: [a, b]` (node names or paths, scenes, class_names or Godot classes): for each pair, whether a detects b and b detects a, why, and the exact mask value that fixes it. `value` says which layers a bit value means, `layers` the value of layer numbers. It is an error when there are problems. Read-only.

between.description: two names: who detects whom, e.g. ["Player", "Enemy"] or ["bullet.tscn", "Hurtbox"]

detail.description: brief (capped lists) or full (everything); default brief

layers.description: layer numbers (1 to 32): the value to write

path.description: project folder, or a file or folder inside it (relative to the server's folder; default: the current project)

value.description: a collision_layer or collision_mask value: which layers it means

name: godot_collisions
title: Physics layers and masks: who detects whom
